text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- More than 300 army officers gathered outside the presidency building in Sofia to protest against a decision by the outgoing Socialist cabinet to increase their salaries only by 60 percent while other state salaries were raised by 100 percent. @

-- Bulgaria's caretaker government expected to be appointed by the president this week will include non-party experts rather than political figures, said Sofia mayor Stefan Sofianski, tipped as the most probable caretaker premier.

-- Bulgaria's caretaker government and the central bank would be ready to start immediate negotiations with an International Monetary Fund mission for the introduction of a currency board system, President Petar Stoyanov said in a letter to the IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus. @

-- Leaders of Bulgarian political parties represented in parliament agreed on an anti-crisis programme to be carried out by the caretaker cabinet, envisaging transparant privatisation, closure of state loss-makers, crackdown on corruption and encouraging foreign investment.
-- Bulgaria's monthly consumer price inflation quickened to 43.8 percent between January 1-25 from 26.9 percent in December, National Statistics Insitute preliminary figures showed.
-- Public transport could stop within days in many Bulgarian cities due to the lack of fuel, directors of eight big state transport comanies said.

-- President Petar Stoyanov met with the Chief Prosecutor Ivan Tatarchev and the head of the Supreme Administrative Court Vladislav Slavov to discuss alleged cases of siphoning of money in recent days.
-- Bulgarians now need some 62,000 levs per month for food alone, up from some 18,000 levs at end-December, the director of Trade Union Social Research Institute Roumyana Kraleva said. @
-- The Japanese government has decided to grant crisis-ridden Bulgaria some $180,000 to ease the plight of the poorest.

-- Bulgarian customs officers seized two kilogrammes of heroin hidden in the fuel tank of a Mercedes car driven by an Albanian citizen at the Gyueshevo checkpoint on the border with Macedonia, a customs official said.
